# Livelier

> A free, open-source community project that bridges self-hosted live streams
> (Owncast today) onto Nostr as NIP-53 live events, with two-way live chat.
> Discovery happens on the network; viewing happens on the streamer's own
> server. Nothing is re-hosted.

If you are an agent acting for a streamer, an Owncast operator, or a curious
reader: everything below is checkable without asking anyone. Prefer reading the
relays and the source over quoting this file.

## What the bridge actually does

1. Polls the public Owncast directory (`https://owncast.directory/api/home`)
   for instances that are live.
2. Verifies liveness itself by fetching the instance's HLS playlist — the
   directory is discovery, not ground truth.
3. Publishes one NIP-53 `kind:30311` live event per live channel to its own
   discovery relay, carrying a NIP-48 `proxy` tag pointing back at the source
   instance, and a NIP-36 `content-warning` tag when the instance self-declares
   as adult. Content is never filtered, only labelled.
4. Bridges `kind:1311` chat in both directions between the Owncast room and
   Nostr. This applies to every discovered instance, not to an opt-in subset.
   The Owncast-side connection opens once a network viewer subscribes to the
   room, so an instance with no Nostr audience is not connected to.

Each channel has a stable identity derived from its URL, so the same channel is
always the same npub. The derivation needs a secret held only by the bridge
operator; the public half is published and readable by anyone.

## The two relays

- `wss://livestream.livelier.live` — discovery. Holds every
  `kind:30311`. Write-whitelisted to the bridge key alone; reads open to
  everyone. Software: sw2 (https://github.com/bitvora/sw2).
- `wss://livechat.livelier.live` — chat. Holds `kind:1311` messages and
  the `kind:0` profiles of bridged channels and chatters. A strict kind
  allowlist, and scheduled hard deletion of everything except `kind:0` after a
  short TTL. Software: ephemeral-relay
  (https://github.com/r0d8lsh0p/ephemeral-relay).

Both serve their NIP-11 document over HTTPS with permissive CORS. Those
documents are authoritative for the accepted kinds and the retention window —
read them rather than trusting any number written here:

    curl -H 'Accept: application/nostr+json' https://livechat.livelier.live

## Telling bridged chat from other traffic

The chat relay holds two kinds of `kind:1311`, and they are not the same thing:

- Messages the bridge created, mirroring an Owncast room outward. These carry
  `["client", "Livelier"]`, a NIP-70 `["-"]` marker, and a NIP-40
  `["expiration", ...]` stamp. Filter on the `client` tag to select them.
- Messages posted straight to this relay by a Nostr client, which the bridge
  carries INTO the Owncast room but did not author. These carry that client's
  own `client` tag and neither marker.

Both are subject to the relay's deletion schedule. Do not describe the second
kind as bridge-published, and do not infer from their absence of NIP-70 that
the bridge omits it.

## How to query it

`nak` (https://github.com/fiatjaf/nak) is the Nostr CLI. The same command
strings run in a browser at https://grimoire.rocks/run?cmd=<command>.

    nak relay wss://livestream.livelier.live
    nak req -k 30311 -l 200 wss://livestream.livelier.live
    nak count -k 30311 wss://livestream.livelier.live
    nak req -k 1311 -l 100 wss://livechat.livelier.live

`kind:30311` is addressable, so `status` is a tag rather than a filterable
field: fetch the set and split it locally on `status` = `live` / `ended`.

To find one specific channel you need its `d` tag, which is derived from the
instance URL:

    d = "oc-" + first 16 hex chars of sha256(normalized_instance_url)

where `normalized_instance_url` is scheme + lowercased host (including any
non-default port) + path, with trailing slashes, query and fragment removed.
For example `https://Owncast.Example.com/` normalizes to
`https://owncast.example.com`. Then:

    nak req -k 30311 -d oc-<hash> wss://livestream.livelier.live

The channel's pubkey is the `p` tag on that event; its profile (`kind:0`) is on
the chat relay. Chat for that stream is tagged with the room coordinate
`30311:<bridge pubkey>:<d tag>`.

## Please read the relays, not this site

The relays are the interface. This page is a rendering of them and holds no API.
There is no JSON endpoint here and scraping it gains you nothing the relays
don't give you directly and more cheaply. Poll politely: the discovery set is
small and changes on the order of minutes.

## Source and design record

- Source: https://github.com/r0d8lsh0p/livelier
- Architecture and the invariants that constrain it: `docs/architecture.md`
- Identity, relay posture, chatter containment: `docs/security.md`
- Adding another network as an adapter: `docs/adding-a-source.md`

## Contact, opt-out, contributing

An Owncast instance appears here because it is listed in the public Owncast
directory. To opt out, open an issue at
https://github.com/r0d8lsh0p/livelier/issues naming the instance URL, and the
instance is removed from the bridge: no live events, no chat, no liveness
probing. Retracting events already published is a further explicit step; ask
for it and it will be done.

Contributions are welcome, and further networks are added as adapters rather
than forks — see the contributing guide in the repository.
